rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~5 at.% Al to an elemental Cr coating, whereas the paper used a multi-principal-element AlTiCrZrNbTa coating with Al contents of 0–25 at.%. The intervention is a different kind of coating system entirely.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies subcritical water (~300°C) and high-temperature steam up to ~850–900°C, while the paper tested isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000°C and 1100°C. The temperature regimes are different, and the hypothesis includes subcritical water which the paper did not test.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes an Al2O3 diffusion barrier to suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion. The paper's mechanism involves a composite Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 surface layer that suppresses oxygen diffusion and preserves adhesion, with excess Al causing intermetallic formation and oxide discontinuity. The general class of protective oxide formation is shared, but the specific pathway and structural mediator differ.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion and improved protection relative to pure Cr. The paper predicted and observed a minimum oxidation rate and oxygen penetration at an intermediate Al content (~10 at.%) with reversal at higher Al, measured via mass gain and oxygen penetration. The property (oxidation/corrosion protection) and direction (improvement with Al addition) align in general terms, but the specific outcome and comparison differ.
